deep.reconstruction: This folio contains no mathematics and nothing by Riemann. It is a printed page, p. 378, of the 'Nachrichten von der G. A. Universität und der Königl. Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen', No. 21, 9 December 1863. The page was filed in the 'R.Primzahlen' bundle, probably because the 1863 issue was kept with Riemann's papers; the 'Riemann ?' note on the previous page suggests the archivist was unsure why it is there. The text continues the annual report given by the permanent secretary, F. Wöhler, at the anniversary session of 5 December 1863. It first finishes the sentence from the previous page: the shorter papers presented had been published in the Nachrichten. It then says that during the year the Society lost ten foreign members or correspondents. The first obituary is of the chemist Eilhard (here spelled 'Eilart') Mitscherlich, who died 28 August 1863. It gives his birth on 7 January 1794 at Neuende near Jever, where his father was a preacher, and his schooling at the Jever Gymnasium under Schlosser, who turned him toward oriental philology. It follows his studies at Heidelberg (1811), Paris (1813) and Göttingen (1814), where he also began natural science and medicine. It mentions the disapproving remark of his uncle, the editor of Horace (Christoph Wilhelm Mitscherlich). It records his move to Berlin in 1818 and his discovery of isomorphism, the lawlike relation between crystal form and chemical composition. It credits this discovery as a foundation of physical chemistry and as raising the importance of crystallography for chemistry; the text continues on p. 379. There are no derivations, formulas or computations to reconstruct.
errors: The printed obituary says Mitscherlich died 'im 69. Lebensjahre'. He was born 7 Jan 1794 and died 28 Aug 1863, so he had completed 69 years and was strictly in his 70th year of life. This is a minor imprecision in the source, not Riemann's.
The name is printed 'Eilart'; the usual spelling is 'Eilhard' Mitscherlich. This is a variant spelling in the source, not a transcription error.

results.what: Obituary notice of Eilhard Mitscherlich in Wöhler's 1863 annual report of the Göttingen Society of Sciences, including the discovery of isomorphism (crystal form vs. chemical composition)
results.usually_credited_to: Eilhard Mitscherlich (1819); the report itself was written by Friedrich Wöhler

deep.surprise_reason: This is a printed society report (an obituary of a chemist) filed among Riemann's papers. It has no mathematical content and no annotation by Riemann, so there is nothing to attribute to him.

checkable.asserts: Mitscherlich (born 7 Jan 1794, died 28 Aug 1863) had completed 69 years at death, so he was in his 70th year rather than his 69th.
